kept.excerpt: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate. The Federal Open Market Committee approved the statement by a 12–0 vote. Inflation remained elevated relative to the Committee's 2 percent goal, in part reflecting supply shocks affecting certain sectors, including energy.
kept.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
kept.relevance: The last FOMC decision before the cutoff establishes a 3.75 percent upper bound and unanimous support for holding rates in June.

kept.excerpt: Both total nonfarm payroll employment (+57,000) and the unemployment rate (4.2 percent) changed little in June, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported. Employment continued to trend up in professional and business services, social assistance, and health care. Leisure and hospitality lost jobs.
kept.relevance: The latest employment report available by the cutoff informs the employment side of the Fed's decision and the potential need to adjust rates.

kept.excerpt: In their consideration of monetary policy at this meeting, all participants supported maintaining the current target range for the federal funds rate. A few participants commented that there was a case for raising the target range, but supported maintaining it at this meeting. Many participants indicated that the appropriate year-end rate would be within or slightly below the current target range, while many others assessed that it would be above that range. Participants noted that their future policy actions would depend on incoming information.
kept.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
kept.relevance: The June minutes reveal both unanimous support for the previous hold and a meaningful division over whether subsequent tightening would be appropriate.

kept.excerpt: Measured inflation stepped up further in March as energy prices surged after the start of the Middle East conflict. Over the 12 months ending in May, the price index for personal consumption expenditures rose 4.1 percent, up substantially from a 2.5 percent pace a year earlier. Core price inflation was 3.4 percent over the 12 months ending in May, up from a 2.8 percent pace a year earlier.
kept.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
kept.relevance: The Fed's contemporaneous report documents elevated headline and core PCE inflation, a potential reason to consider tightening despite the recent pattern of holds.

kept.excerpt: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers decreased 0.4 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in June after rising 0.5 percent in May. This decline was the largest one-month decrease since April 2020. Over the last 12 months, the all-items index increased 3.5 percent before seasonal adjustment. The energy index fell 5.7 percent in June after rising 3.9 percent in May.
kept.relevance: The latest consumer inflation release before the cutoff provides fresh evidence of cooling prices that could reduce pressure for an immediate rate increase.

kept.excerpt: The members of our Committee have no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation. And we share a resolute commitment to restoring price stability. This was the focus of our June meeting, at which we decided to hold the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent. America's labor market appears broadly stable.
kept.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System — Chairman Kevin Warsh
kept.relevance: The chair's testimony immediately before the cutoff reiterates the existing rate range and inflation commitment while describing a stable labor market.
